Lotion: permitted.
21 CFR 73.2150(b) states: "Dihydroxyacetone may be safely used in amounts consistent with good manufacturing practice in externally applied cosmetics intended solely or in part to impart a color to the human body." [2].
Use limit: no percentage is stated; the amount is consistent with good manufacturing practice [2].
21 CFR 73.2150(a) states: "The color additive dihydroxyacetone shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 73.1150 (a)(1) and (b)." [1].
21 CFR 73.2150(c) states: "The labeling of the color additive and any mixtures prepared therefrom intended solely or in part for coloring purposes shall conform to the requirements of § 70.25 of this chapter." [3].
21 CFR 73.2150(d) states: "Certification of this color additive is not necessary for the protection of the public health and therefore batches thereof are exempt from the requirements of section 721(c) of the act." [4].
21 CFR 70.3(v) states: "The terms externally applied drugs and externally applied cosmetics mean drugs or cosmetics applied only to external parts of the body and not to the lips or any body surface covered by mucous membrane." [5].
